title: The home of the resolved session labels, the target of the conflict incident and the team and region read behind the scope line are not specified for the sign-on app slice
source: RWB-E1-022 sections 4, 5, 8, 11, 12 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 14, 20, 35 and 41; RWB-PLT-N006-INF (gateway-bff Redis session store); ADR-010; FSD P4 v3 A2.1 and A2.14; Ownership Map (queue, queue_member owned by P3)
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) The legacy story held the resolved SessionContext in the process and kept the matrix and conflict versions on it until the session ended (legacy BR7), while the target keeps the session in the Redis store of gateway-bff and gives rwb-access no session table (ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 20); no source states which resolved values that session record carries, or whether rwb-access resolves again on every call, so the home of the version labels AC9 depends on is a working read. (b) AC6 requires the system to raise an incident to the security administrator queue; no source of this read set names an incident queue, an incident operation or a target service for that incident, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no event and no incident path, so the incident has no addressee. (c) The TEAM and REGION scopes name team and region codes, and the team rows are rwb-case's under the Ownership Map, while no source names the read that returns a person's team and region codes: RWB-P3-E1019-CON is the only named contract over that data and its operation is not specified.
evidence: RWB-E1-022 section 8 BR7 ("A session keeps the matrix and conflict versions it resolved at sign-in until it ends") and section 5 X4 ("an incident is raised to the security administrator; the refusal is logged"); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 P4 OUT line (schema rwb_access: Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log; topic rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged) and slide 20 (gateway-bff DB Redis: sessions only; no business data); ADR-010 (no token store); Ownership Map queue row (owner P3)
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-022 AC6, AC9, section 4 steps 6 and 9
owner_role: rwb-access service owner with the architecture review
proposed: rwb-access resolves per call and hands the role set, the scope and the two version labels to the edge for its session record; the conflict incident rides the refusal fact with reason code ROLE_CONFLICT; the team and region codes are read through the roles-and-teams operation of RWB-P3-E1019-CON

title: The two operation paths and their request and answer payloads are not specified by any source for the access contract of rwb-access
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 20 and 41; Ownership Map v1 (no path row for authorise, me/permissions, doa-limits or masking-policies); RWB-E1-022 section 12; TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 (API-P4-012 GET /me/session)
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operations authorise and me/permissions and the Ownership Map has no path row for either, so neither the base nor the path suffix is a map row and the base of section R4 is applied by rule instead. (b) No source fixes the request and the answer of the authorise operation: the legacy story published a Java method check(SessionContext, CapabilityArea, Right) and a resolve method over a SessionContext type inside one process, and the slide names the inputs role, scope and DoA without a payload, so the fields the contract publishes are stated by the contract and not copied. (c) The only published description of a resolved session is API-P4-012 GET /me/session, which belongs to the role-to-permission contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON and not to this contract, so the shape of the me/permissions answer beyond roles, scope, matrix version and conflict version is not fixed by any source.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 P4 IN line ("REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) · GET /me/permissions · GET /doa-limits · /masking-policies") and slide 41 ("First API path /authorise"); Ownership Map v1 api list (GET /admin/roles and GET /admin/access-log are the only P4 path rows); RWB-E1-022 section 12 (Published interface AccessCheck, SessionResolver)
owner_role: contract owner of rwb-access with the consuming squads
proposed: Publish POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions under the base of section R4 and DP-13, with the payload stated by the contract, the operation named by the slide and the two version labels in every answer

title: The rwb-access login name, the ACE group source behind a mapping row and the column set of the three library objects are not specified for the schema slice
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20 and 29; Ownership Map v1 (role, permission, role_conflict owned by P4; outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key library objects, asm ASM-A6-tables-8); FSD P4 v3 A2.1 and A2.14; TSD P4 v3 T3.0, T3.1 and T3.3; RWB-E1-022 section 13
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 11 Data; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) Section R4 and Architecture v5 slide 29 fix one login per service and show rwb_case as the pattern, and no source fixes the login name of rwb-access, so the grantee of this schema is a working read. (b) FSD P4 v3 A2.1 reads the group mapping from v_ace_iam_group (ACE, iam_group, RWB-ACE-001) and states that the mapping is not a Workbench column, while TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines role.entra_group and the legacy story and RWB-P4-AD001-CON keep the mapping rows there; the column set of the view is in no source of this read set, and the P1 contract that would carry it is not yet published. (c) The column set and the keys of outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key are published by the event platform template (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON) and are restated by no source of this read set, so the schema story applies the template without naming a column.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.1 field catalog ("v_ace_iam_group.entra_group | Entra ID group mapped to the role, read from ACE (iam_group, RWB-ACE-001); not a Workbench column") and A2.1.4.3 AC-EXC-P4-001-04 ("no v_ace_iam_group row maps RWB-SIT-LEGACY01 to an active role"); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role table (DF-REF-039 entra_group, source Entra ID); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 (one login per service, rwb_case shown); Ownership Map v1 ruling on outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key (asm ASM-A6-tables-8)
area: Access schema, grants and library objects
owner_role: ACE database engineer with the rwb-access service owner and the P1 data owner
proposed: Grant to a login named rwb_access as the section R4 pattern and let the platform DB story set the real name and pool; keep the mapping rows in role.entra_group with TSD P4 v3 outranking FSD v3 under R-PREC and read the ACE group facts only through the P1 contract; apply the event platform template unchanged

title: Missing and conflicting values in the rwb-access matrix and masking slice (RWB-P4-E1037-APP)
description: (a) No source states the path or the right of the masking-policy operation: Arch v5 slide 14 names /masking-policies, while the API Specification v4 and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A list no such path, so the base rule of §R4 is applied. (b) The roster conflicts: the legacy criteria count 54 roles against 14 capability areas for the 756 permission rows of AC1, while TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists 42 role codes, so the count of a version is not fixed by the sources. (c) The payload of rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 is named by Arch v5 slide 14 and by no schema. (d) WP B-P4-01 carries no DB story for RWB-E1-037, so the origin of the five rwb_access baseline objects is not stated. (e) The rwb-case case contract that the criteria call (GET /queues, GET /cases, GET /cases/{caseId}, POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer) has no C row in this WP, so the fake is taken as that contract's fake.
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A and T6.1; Physical Schema v6; legacy RWB-E1-037 sections 7, 12 and 16
evidence: Slide 14 lists IN /masking-policies with no path; API Specification v4 has x-module P4 for /admin/reference-loads, /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve and /admin/roles only, and no /masking-policies entry; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists 42 role codes; RWB-E1-037 AC1 names 756 rows and section 2 names 54 roles against 14 capability areas; no schema for AccessPolicyChanged beyond the event name on slide 14.
area: P4 access: permission matrix, masking rules and identity boundary
proposed: Fix the masking-policy path as /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies with Reference data R; count the rows of a version from the approved file, with 756 rows at 54 roles and a roster that grows to 54 by go-live; publish AccessPolicyChanged with the change kind, the version label and the effective date and no value; state that the rwb_access baseline is the service template's V0001; take the rwb-case case contract's fake as the mock of the criteria.

title: The load, approve and masking-policy contract of rwb-access has a missing path and a conflicting owner (RWB-P4-E1037-CON)
description: (a) Conflict: the R-PREC default ruling gives parameters and reference data (RWB-E1-043) to P3 rwb-case, while the API Specification v4 declares x-module P4 for /admin/reference-loads and /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A names them as API-P4-005 and API-P4-006, so the owner of the load path is not settled by the sources. (b) Missing: Arch v5 slide 14 names /masking-policies but no source gives it a path or a right, and the Ownership Map has no path row for it. (c) Missing: the payload of rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 is named only by the event name on Arch v5 slide 14. (d) Missing: no source fixes the exact answer shape (field list and order) of the masking-policy read beyond the fields of masking_rule.
source: Template and Rules v1 §R3 default rulings and §R5.5 DP-06 and DP-07; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 x-module P4; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A; Ownership Map; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14
evidence: Plan Appendix R §R3 gives parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case; API Specification v4 lines for /admin/reference-loads and /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve carry x-module P4 and x-capability Reference data C and A; TSD P4 v3 T-A lists API-P4-005 and API-P4-006; slide 14 lists /masking-policies with no base, right or schema.
area: P4 access: access and masking contract
proposed: Keep the two load and approve operations for this service's own permission and masking tables on /api/recovery/access/v1, with the generic reference-load path for lists, queues, timers, templates and parameters with rwb-case; publish /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies with Reference data R; publish AccessPolicyChanged with the change kind, the version and the effective date and no personal value; answer the matrix read from both role slices under one contract.

title: Local decision-record table, legacy break-glass path and the composition of the entry actions are not fixed by the sources
description: (a) No source names the local decision-record table that the DP-03 library creates in rwb_access, so the entry is named by its contract and never by an invented table name. (b) The legacy criteria call POST /admin/break-glass while the Ownership Map and TSD P4 v3 publish POST /admin/break-glass-grants, so the criterion keeps the legacy spelling and the operation is the published one. (c) The composition of the actions element of an entry for a refusal and for an export, its keys and their order, is not fixed field by field in any source.
source: Ownership Map v1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and appendix T-A; Architecture v5 slide 28; legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 7, 11 and 12
evidence: The Ownership Map has no row for a decision-record table; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 declares role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit only; the legacy section 12 declares POST /admin/break-glass-grants as new while its criteria call POST /admin/break-glass.
proposed: Confirm the library table name with the DP-03 owner, keep the legacy path in the criterion as an alias of the published operation, and fix the actions keys in the contract before the endpoint is frozen.

title: The grant end and read paths, the 401 business message id and the full grant answer are not fixed by the sources
description: (a) No source names the end and read operations of a break-glass grant, so they follow the base rule of DP-13 at /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}/end and /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}. (b) No source gives the business message id of an expired session, so a 401 carries the gateway-bff session envelope and no business id. (c) The grant answer beyond grantId, incidentReference, capabilityArea, right, scope, startsAt and endsAt, and the grant state field, are not fixed.
source: Ownership Map v1; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A (API-P4-013); Architecture v5 slide 11; legacy RWB-E1-039 section 12
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A declares API-P4-013 POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/break-glass-grants only and no end or read operation; the legacy error list has no 401 message id; the legacy response lists seven fields and no state.
proposed: Confirm the two paths and the grant state field with the security administrator, and add the expired-session message id to the message catalogue.

title: No source names the grant table, its two-person constraint, the retention period or the partition granularity of the access log
description: (a) No source names a break-glass grant table in rwb_access or the constraint that keeps one active grant per person, so the table is break_glass_grant with a unique partial constraint on the active grant of an actor. (b) The retention period and the partition granularity of the access log are not set; DL26 is open, so both are parameter rows and the action is a partition drop. (c) The local decision-record table has no name in the Ownership Map and the grantee login name is not in the source.
source: Ownership Map v1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and appendix T-B (DL26); legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 11 and 13
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 declares no access-log table and no grant table; the legacy section 13 states that the story has no table of its own; T-B records DL26 as open for retention periods.
proposed: Confirm the grant table, its columns and the constraint with the security administrator, and set the retention period at DL26 with Compliance before the first production release.

title: Alert routes, thresholds, Kafka ACL set, retry cadence and secret names are not fixed by the sources
description: (a) No source names the alert routes or the thresholds of a failed or refused access-log write and of break-glass use, so they are deployment values with a parameter row behind them and the routes in force. (b) The Kafka ACL set and the retry cadence of rwb.decision-record.v1 are not fixed; the set follows the producer rule of the platform and the platform retry topics. (c) The secret names, their key references and the deployment topology values are not in the source.
source: Architecture v5 slides 20, 30 and 42; TSD P4 v3 T5.1 and appendix T-B (DL11); legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 5 and 14
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 gives the topic and the retry rule without a cadence; T-B leaves the non-functional targets open under DL11; the legacy section 5 names the platform administrator queue but no alert route or threshold.
proposed: Agree the two routes and the thresholds with the security administrator and the platform on-call rota, and record the secret names and topology values in the platform secret store and the values files.

title: The partner identity resolution operation, its claim set, its answer schema, the scope type PLACED and the lifetime of an answer are specified by no source
description: Four values an rwb-access slice of the partner identity resolution needs are absent from every source. (a) No operation exists for the resolution: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none is a partner identity operation, API Specification v4 declares no partner identity path with x-module P4, and Architecture v5 slide 14 names only /authorise, /me/permissions, /doa-limits and /masking-policies, so the path, the method and the access rule are fixed here from the base rule and carried as an assumption. (b) The claim set the external gateway supplies and the answer it receives have no schema in any source: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines partner_user with DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists only the RW- roles, so the claim names partnerIdentityRef, partnerId, partnerRoleCodes, firmPanelStatus, firmContractEnd, amr, route and tokenExpiry and the answer names roles, scope, matrixVersion, maskingVersion, expiry and decision are fixed here and each maps to a DF field or to a gateway claim. (c) The scope type PLACED is named by legacy RWB-E2-019 and by FSD P6 AC-P6-013-01 but is not a value of LOV-SCOPE in TSD P4 v3 T3.2, which holds OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, and no source says whether PLACED is a scope of the role model or a descriptor of a partner session; the answer carries it as a session descriptor and does not add it to the role default-scope list. The lifetime of an answer beyond the gateway token lifetime is also absent: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes a five-minute token lifetime for the partner edge and no source states how long a resolved answer may live, so the answer expires no later than the token. Nothing here blocks a build, because every value is a claim, a row, a parameter or a reference value read at run time and no literal appears in code.
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 14, 20, 29, 35 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1 and appendix T-A; API Specification v4 (no x-module P4 partner path); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 (REQ-ACA-012 and the role class only); FSD P6 Communications v3 AC-P6-013-01 (scope PLACED); legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 14; RWB-PLT-N007-INF section 11 (token lifetime); RWB-PLT-N007-INF 12.2 (the rwb-partner upstream)
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 12; section 7 AC6 and AC9; section 11 Data; section 12.1, 12.2 and 12.3; section 13 Components and Build steps 1 to 5; section 14 Validation and messages
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 reads API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no partner identity row; API Specification v4 carries x-module S9 on /partners and on the four /partner/instructions paths and no x-module P4 partner path; Architecture v5 slide 14 reads rwb-access IN as POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines partner_user (DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217) without a status, a contract end or a claim set; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE reads OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL with no PLACED value; FSD P6 v3 AC-P6-013-01 reads the session holds role PT-LAWFIRM, scope PLACED and partner LF-0012; RWB-PLT-N007-INF section 11 reads the access token lifetime as 5 minutes; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 12 defines a ScopeFilter with type PLACED, partnerId and instructionTypes and a PartnerStatus published interface, and names no operation, no claim and no answer schema.
area: rwb-access partner identity resolution: operation, claim set, answer schema and answer lifetime
owner_role: Solution architect, P4 rwb-access with the external gateway owner
proposed: At the RWB-P4-E2019-CON contract review, confirm the resolution path on the P4 base, the claim names and the answer field names with the external gateway owner and the rwb-partner owner, and register the operation in the API specification and in TSD P4 appendix T-A with its schema. State in TSD P4 v3 T3.2 whether PLACED is a session scope descriptor or a role default scope. State the lifetime of a resolved answer against the token lifetime of the partner edge. Nothing here blocks the build: this story reads every value at run time and writes the placeholder wherever a literal would appear.

title: The contract of the partner identity resolution names no path, no claim or answer field, no refusal-to-status mapping and no statement of its absent events in any source
description: Four contract values are absent from every source. (a) The operation path is named nowhere: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and API Specification v4 declares no x-module P4 partner path, so the document fixes POST /partner-identities/resolve on the base /api/recovery/access/v1 from the base rule and duplicates no path of rwb-partner. (b) The claim and answer field names have no source: the legacy story publishes a Java interface with ScopeFilter and PartnerStatus and no wire shape, so the fields are fixed here and each is mapped to DF-REF-035, DF-REF-037, DF-REF-043, DF-REF-044, DF-REF-202, DF-REF-213 to DF-REF-215, DF-PRT-005 and DF-PRT-006 or to a gateway claim. (c) The mapping of a refusal to an HTTP status is not stated: the legacy story gives MSG-P4-001 on four different conditions, MSG-P4-005 without a reason code, MSG-P4-006 with an incident and MSG-P4-008 without a status, so the document fixes 400 for a malformed claim set, 401 for MSG-P4-001 and MSG-P4-005, 403 for MSG-P4-006 and MSG-P4-008 and 503 for MSG-P7-003. The absence of a published or consumed event is also unstated: Architecture v5 slide 14 calls rwb-access a reference-data owner with no event on the input side and names AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged as its only events, and no source says that a resolution publishes nothing, so the document states the absence and names the record as the DP-03 library event. Nothing here blocks the build, because the baseline is a document and its fakes.
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 41 and 42; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T5.3, T6.1 and appendix T-A; API Specification v4; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and AC-EXC-P4-001-03; legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 5, 7, 12 and 14
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 1 to 11; section 7 AC1 to AC6; section 11 Data; section 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4 and 12.7; section 13 Build steps 1 to 8; section 14 Validation and messages
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 has no partner identity operation and T-A.2 defines no partner schema; API Specification v4 declares x-module S9 on /partners and on the four /partner/instructions paths; Architecture v5 slide 14 reads rwb-access EVT as (none: reference data owner) and its OUT events as AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged only, and slide 11 fixes one RFC 9457 problem detail per error; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 names the conflict refusal with MSG-P4-006 and no status; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 5 gives MSG-P4-001 for no binding and for a bank identity on the partner route, MSG-P4-005 for no second factor without a status, MSG-P4-008 for a firm that has exited without a status, and MSG-P4-003 with status 404 for an instruction of another firm; section 12 publishes Java interfaces only.
area: rwb-access contract baseline of the partner identity resolution
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-access with the external gateway owner and the rwb-partner service owner
proposed: At the contract review, register the resolution operation and its two schemas in the API specification and in TSD P4 appendix T-A, agree the refusal-to-status table with the gateway owner and the message catalogue, and state in the document that the capability publishes no event and consumes none. Nothing here blocks the build: the baseline is a document with fakes, and the review freezes the names before the resolver and the DMZ slice depend on them.

title: The certificate profile, the rotation and revocation of the rwb-access hop, the numeric rate limit and the namespace and service names of the DMZ hop are specified by no source
description: Four infrastructure values of the hop from the partner gateway to rwb-access are absent from every source. (a) The certificate profile of the hop, its lifetime, its rotation window and the revocation propagation are named for the partner client at the gateway by RWB-PLT-N007-INF and are not stated for the gateway-to-rwb-access hop, so this story applies one profile to both ends and fixes the rotation inside an overlap window with a suspension at the deadline. (b) The per-client rate limit, its burst, its window and its retry hint on the resolution route are stated by no source: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes per-client limits for the partner portal route and NFR-003 sizes the partner population, so this story adopts the platform limit of the gateway and states the values it tests against. (c) The namespace, the service name and the port of rwb-access are not fixed by any source read: Architecture v5 slide 29 fixes the schema and the login and names no Kubernetes service, so the story writes namespace rwb-recovery and the rwb-access service port as the deployment defines them and names no number. The egress and ingress policy shape is also absent: no source states a NetworkPolicy object, so the story fixes one namespace, one service and one port in both directions, deny by default. Nothing here blocks a build, because every value is configuration applied by the infrastructure team and the platform defaults are recorded as the values the tests use.
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 29 and 35; RWB-PLT-N007-INF sections 3, 11, 12.2 and 13; NFR-003; NFR-056; legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 1, 4 and 19
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 5 Exception paths X1 to X9; section 7 AC2 to AC5; section 11 Data; section 12.2 and 12.9; section 13 Build steps 1 to 8; section 14 Validation and messages
evidence: RWB-PLT-N007-INF section 11 reads the certificate as valid for 12 months and the revocation as effective within 30 days at the latest, for the partner client; its section 12.2 names rwb-partner as the only upstream and no rwb-access hop; Architecture v5 slide 29 reads one login per service in one ACE database and names no Kubernetes service or port; slide 35 reads every call encrypted and identified both ways with no lifetime; NFR-003 reads about 50 partner users online in the busiest hour of about 320 named users; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 19 leaves the architecture change of the external access out of scope and names no certificate, no policy and no limit.
area: DMZ hop from the partner gateway to rwb-access: certificate, policy and rate limit
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the security design authority
proposed: At the security design authority review of RWB-PLT-N007-INF, extend the certificate profile and the rotation window to the rwb-access hop, record the per-client limit and its burst for the resolution route in the gateway configuration baseline, and publish the namespace, service and port of rwb-access with the platform deployment so the NetworkPolicy names them from a source. Nothing here blocks the build: every value is configuration and the recorded defaults are the values the tests use.

title: The mapping version columns, the mapping operations, the environment code and the group names are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-001); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: (a) `role` carries `entra_group` (DF-REF-039) and no version label and no valid-from and valid-to dates, while legacy AC3 needs a new mapping version with a valid from date; (b) the mapping read, the mapping change and the version read have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, whose only role read is GET /admin/roles (API-P4-007), and the legacy Endpoints table names GET and POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions, which belong to the rule-version stories and not to a group mapping; (c) the environment code of a deployment and the codes beyond SIT are named by no source, although the story maps a group to one role in each environment; (d) no source states whether a mapping version needs a second approval; (e) the final Entra ID group names are the open bank IAM naming decision DL40; (f) the composite route specification and the field list of SCR-43 for the mapping are not stated.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039, no date column) and appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles only); legacy RWB-AD-001 Endpoints table (GET and POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions) and Permission checks table (Rules and parameters R, C); FSD P4 v3 change note and A2.3 field catalog; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 (P4 owns the roles as data and the access log).
proposed: Carry the mapping version label and the valid-from and valid-to dates with the role rows of the environment in `rwb_access` and add them by this key's migration; fix the three operations under `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin` with Platform administration R for the reads and C for the change; read the environment code as a parameter through the parameters contract of rwb-case; treat a mapping version as needing no second approval and record every change in the decision log; use the legacy group name `RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN` until DL40 fixes the names; leave the screen side of SCR-43 to the composite route owner.

title: The mapping contract shapes, its three paths and its event payload are not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-001); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: (a) the field names, types and lengths of the mapping row, the mapping version and the page, and the version label and the two effective dates, have no physical definition in any source; (b) the paths, the rights, the request and answer shapes and the error responses of the three operations have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A; (c) the parameter code that carries the environment and the environment codes beyond SIT are not named; (d) no source names the payload of an access-policy event for a mapping change, and the decision code of a mapping entry (AC-CHG) is this revision's own; (e) the deprecation window of a published field and the retention of the contract fakes are not stated.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and appendix T-A.1 (no mapping operation, no version or date column); Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 43 (rwb.access.events.v1 carries AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged only, with the cache-refresh consumers); FSD P4 v3 A2.3 and A2.17 (role administration by the security administrator); ownership map (role and permission are P4's; parameters and reference data are P3's).
area: Access and role administration; API contract
proposed: Fix the three operations and the three schemas in the contract baseline of this key, with Platform administration R for the reads and C for the change, one problem envelope with the seven message IDs and the four fakes; declare the change as `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind MAPPING on `rwb.access.events.v1` and the entry on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; leave the field-level detail to the contract review and record the deprecation and retention decisions with the platform contract owner.
